title: VPC masquerade / NAT debug daily notes - Sep 28 2026
body:
Context:
We spun up a fresh VPC for Customer Zenith to run a private deployment in their Azure subscription. Early validation showed node egress failures when the onprem connector tried to pull model artifacts (S3-compatible endpoint via a transit gateway). Suspect: inconsistent SNAT/masquerade rules on host vs container network, and path MTU/DF behavior on their firewall.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner)
- Miguel (network lead)
- Hannah (install engineer)
- Omar (SRE support)
- Priya (customer eng)

Summary of what happened today:
- 09:20: customer reported 504s fetching model shards during warm start.
- 09:35 we confirmed curl from host -> upstream S3 succeeded, but containerized runtime failed with connection resets.
- 10:10 captured tcpdump on host and inside container. Observed TCP SYN/ACK sequence where server resets after packet larger than MSS (suspect DF).
- 11:00 repro on our lab (minion in their VNet using same iptables rules) — confirmed issue is dependent on SNAT applied by host-level iptables MASQUERADE for pod CIDR.
- 13:30 tested removing MASQUERADE rule and using SNAT to a fixed egress IP (acceptance test) — patchy, but more stable for big transfers.

Key hypotheses:
- Host MASQUERADE + container iptables conntrack mis-translation when firewall rewrites headers (Cisco ASA weirdness) leading to mid-transfer resets.
- Path MTU discovery blocked by firewall setting DF on some middleboxes; large token-chunk transfers hit the DF and cause ICMP blackhole.
- Azure vnet peering + third-party transit (customer transit appliance) rewrites TCP options and breaks conntrack expectation on host.

Commands & artifacts we used (notes to self):
- host tcpdump: tcpdump -i eth0 host <artifact-host> and port 443 -w /tmp/host-09-28.pcap
- container tcpdump via nsenter: nsenter --target <pid> --net tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ctr-09-28.pcap
- iptables check: iptables -t nat -S | grep MASQUERADE
- test curl: curl -v --limit-rate 1M https://artifact-host/path/to/shard
- conntrack dump: conntrack -L | grep <artifact-host-ip>

What worked (temporary mitigations):
- Pinning egress NAT to a single static SNAT IP on the host reduced connection resets during large shard downloads.
- Splitting shard downloads into smaller ranges (<= 64KB) avoided DF/MSS failures in our repro (not acceptable long-term).
- Asking customer to temporarily bypass third-party transit appliance (they did for 20m) — downloads succeeded during bypass.

Open blockers / decisions needed from customer/network team:
- Can they allow ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages across the transit path? Firewall currently drops those.
- Can we schedule a maintenance window to test removing MASQUERADE on a single host and use static SNAT?
- Customer needs to share configuration for their transit appliance (firmware, NAT mode) — we have partial screenshots but need full config.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: write concise runbook patch for static SNAT fallback and rollback steps (ETA: 2026-09-30).
- Miguel: build a reproducible test harness that emulates the customer's transit rewrite (use VyOS + iptables) and validate conntrack behavior (ETA: 2026-10-04).
- Hannah: update installer to expose a flag --egress-snat-mode with values [masquerade|static-snat] and add telemetry (ETA: prototype 2026-10-06).
- Omar: add pcap collection hooks to install-runner (automate capture when artifact fetch fails) and push to S3 for postmortem (ETA: 2026-10-02).
- Priya: coordinate with Zenith networking team to confirm ICMP policy and schedule 2-hour window next week for an A/B test (ETA: coordinate by 2026-09-30).

Runbook notes (to fold into confluence):
- Before changing NAT mode, capture host/container pcaps and conntrack snapshots.
- If switching to static SNAT: ensure the SNAT IP is routeable through the transit path and ACLs allow it.
- If firewall blocks ICMP fragmentation-needed: recommend enabling DF fallback via lowering MTU on host veth (quick patch) while longer-term fix is to allow ICMP or tune transit appliance.

Risks & questions:
- If we default to static SNAT in installer, multi-tenant customers might hit IP exhaustion in NAT pools. Need clear limits and telemetry.
- Does the dedicated deploy SLA allow us to change host iptables? (Legal/ops question)
- Is this a pattern likely to impact other customers using middlebox transit appliances? (We saw 1 other customer with similar symptom last quarter.)

Notes to self / brainstorming:
- Consider adding a small MTU-aware probe during install that negotiates safe chunk size with artifact host.
- Long term: move artifact hosting to a CDN in-customer-region or use multistream chunking with reconnect semantics so single packet loss doesn't blow whole transfer.

Meeting close:
- Quick sync tomorrow 09:00 to review runbook draft and agree on A/B test window.
- Keep Jira ENG-4821 updated with test results and attach pcaps.

Unresolved:
- Customer transit appliance model + config (still pending).
- Formal decision whether installer default should change for all onprem deployments (needs product + legal input).
